In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of glycation cross-links is a complex process and the results depend on the type of sugar and the bone tissue used.

the glycation of bone tissue in vitro by glucose and ribose results in the formation of different types of AGEs and crosslinks, and that the glycation efficiency of bone matrix proteins is higher in cancellous bone than cortical bone.

glycation of human bone matrix proteins is not only dependent on the type of sugar used for glycation but also on the type of bone (cortical or cancellous), donor age and gender, and the type of AGEs analyzed (e.g., AGEs or PEN).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glycation of human cortical and cancellously bone captures differences in the formation of Maillard reaction products between glucose and ribose.
ribosylation of bone matrix proteins may be more important than glucosylation for the development of bone pathologies, and that the use of ribose in food supplements should be avoided.
ribosylation is a better tool to study the formation of PEN, while glucosylation is a more suitable model to study glycation of bone proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ribosylation of bone proteins is much more efficient than glucosylation in the formation of AGEs and, in particular, pentosidine, which may explain why bone pathologies related with ribosylation are more severe than glucosylation.

glycation of bone by different sugars can be used to study the formation of advanced Maillard reaction products, and to assess differences in the glycation progression between different sugars and different bone tissues.
the use of glucose as a sugar in the food industry and in drinks may lead to the formation of AGEs and crosslinks in bone, whereas the use of ribose may result in a more pronounced formation of PEN.
